$comment: The source of sf-drawer's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/drawer (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

snap.summary: A bottom sheet's resting height: its content's, half the room under the app bar, or all of it.

controlled.summary: An outside switch (an element naming the drawer in aria-controls) opens and closes the panel: no close button while that switch is on screen.

close-label.summary: Empty: the text of the page's language ("Close drawer" in English).

stack-offset.summary: How much of each drawer below shows past the one above it at the same edge, as a length (for example var(--sf-space-4)). A drawer stands depth × offset in from its edge, where depth counts the open, undocked drawers below it at that edge. Empty: drawers lie flush.

dock-breakpoint.summary: From what width of the dock host (or the window, without a host) a docked drawer is a column of the page; narrower, it floats over the page and is modal (unless modal=false). A length in rem, em or px. Empty: the --sf-drawer-dock-breakpoint variable where the drawer stands, else 48rem.

block-start.summary: Where this panel starts from the top (an app bar's height); the --sf-drawer-block-start variable sets it for every panel.

gutter.summary: The inline gutter the head and the body share, as a length (for example var(--sf-space-3)), so the title and the content start on one axis. Empty: the drawer's own, space-1. A theme may set --sf-drawer-gutter instead.

panel-style.summary: Declarations set on the panel itself, for the custom properties it reads -- its background, radius, shadow. A consumer painting its content a different colour than the panel leaves the head and the gutters in the other one.

open.summary: Opens the Drawer, or brings it to the front when already open. Dispatches sf-drawer-open (cancelable) and later sf-drawer-opened unless options.emit is false. Returns the element.

close.summary: Closes the Drawer and returns focus (to the opener when it is the top layer; a drawer closing under another layer moves no focus). Dispatches sf-drawer-close (cancelable) and sf-drawer-closed unless options.emit is false; options.reason says why (close, escape, outside, cancelled, api; api by default). Returns the element.

toggle.summary: Calls close() when open, open() otherwise. Returns the element.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript (SfDrawer.template()), the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-drawer for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail, split (the old detail from the element's adapter), page-trigger (a page attribute the drawer reads, no shim), retired (no new name; kept and noted by the component until the date).

x-summary: Workspace side panel that keeps the page usable: docked column or modeless panel. Modal side panels belong to sf-modal; the modal Drawer mode is deprecated.
x-renamed: settings.title → heading: "title" is a property of HTMLElement.prototype (§3.1, §16 item 26), alias dated
x-decisions: alias-conflict: vocabulary §5.1 decides drawer:snap → sf-drawer-snapped, a fact of the component (the alias table's sf-drawer-snap is the bare verb of a request the drawer never waits on); the converter's sf-drawer-snap never shipped and gets no row.

detail-adapter: §8 takes page elements out of detail, so the new names carry {drawerId, …} only; each old drawer:* name keeps its old detail (component, drawer, root added) through a split row and the element's detail adapter (sfAliasAdapters). Larena and bx-simai.main listen to drawer:after-open and drawer:after-close (vocabulary §9.2).
version: 1.6.0 → 1.7.0, a minor while the renamed members hold dated aliases (§4.10); added unsaved, dismissible and the snapped detail field.

existing-aliases: compatibility.deprecations folds into aliases.json as documentation rows: the page triggers data-sf-drawer-open/-close/-toggle stay as aliases of data-sf-action (§16.10) and of data-drawer with aria-controls; the modal-like default without docked keeps its own deprecation in the change journal (no alias kind: it is a recommendation, not a name).
template: templates.default names the Lit template in index.js (template()), the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json plus the docked column, the bottom sheet and the outside close button; probe.json drives Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape (gate 16).

css-variables: the seven variables docs.md and the sheet already promise (background, colour, overlay, gutter, block start, dock breakpoint, z-index); the portal carries their computed values from the host (§19.1). --sf-drawer-radius and --sf-drawer-width stay internal: the sheet sets them per size.
side-effects: the panel draws at the end of body or of its [data-sf-overlay-container] (portal) and, when modal and not docked, locks the page through the layer stack's one lease (locks-page).
layer: kind panel (§19.1); a modal drawer traps focus, a docked or modeless one does not (updateLayer re-declares it when modal or docked changes).

modal on a narrow screen (1.8.0, q-a49e2045c1, asked by ui-chat): the existing boolean modal (default true) now reaches a docked drawer that floats -- the dock host or the window narrower than its dock-breakpoint -- so it traps focus, shows its scrim, locks the page, closes on Escape and gives focus back like any modal drawer (§19.2); a docked column stays modeless, and modal="false" keeps a drawer modeless everywhere. No new setting: an enum modal (auto|always|never) would break modal="false" and the boolean property, and "always" means nothing for a column; the breakpoint is the one the drawer already docks by. A drawer that starts or stops floating while open declares it to the stack again (syncModal).
slots: the drawer places the page's own nodes (the content into its body, slot="edge" beside the panel) and never copies them (§4.5); the converter's slot "default" is the content slot.
dismissing: the close request carries {reason, unsaved} (§19.3); dismissible=false removes escape and outside like close-on-esc and close-on-overlay, never an explicit action.
instance ids (§7.1.1, simai/ui-source#41): a drawer without id or drawer-id takes its path id (sf-drawer-<n> in document order) instead of a random one.

version 1.8.1: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

dock_host.description: A host element marked data-sf-drawer-dock-host receives padding-inline-start/end equal to the summed widths of open docked drawers per logical side, published as --sf-drawer-dock-inline-start/end on the document root. A host narrower than the drawer's threshold (dock-breakpoint, else --sf-drawer-dock-breakpoint, else 48rem) keeps zero padding for it. A toggle switch outside the drawer (data-drawer="toggle" naming it in aria-controls, or data-sf-drawer-toggle) hides and shows a docked column and carries aria-expanded. A docked drawer with the room is a column of the page (data-sf-drawer-column="true" on its root): surface-0, no shadow; without the room it floats over the page with the raised surface and shadow. --sf-drawer-background overrides both.

slots.description: The named slots the consumer fills.

default.description: The drawer's content, moved into the scrolling body.

edge.description: Stands beside the panel, on its outer edge, where the panel's own clipping cannot reach it.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-drawer for a workspace side panel next to a page that stays usable: docked (page content shifts, both sides at once; below its dock-breakpoint it floats over the page as a modal panel) or modal=false (overlapping, no scrim, no focus trap). For a modal side panel use sf-modal with position="inline-start|inline-end".
do_not: Do not use a modal sf-drawer for new interfaces; use sf-modal with a side position
Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
Do not use overlay as a substitute for modal semantics
Do not pass literal design dimensions when a standard size or Framework token exists

Content

accessibility.focus: Modal Drawer moves focus inside, traps Tab on the top instance and restores an available opener. Modeless Drawer does not trap focus or lock the page. Docked Drawer is a named role=region column: no focus trap, no scroll lock; Escape closes the top instance.

deprecations.path: modal (default mode without docked or modal=false)

changes: Add docked: a modeless role=region column that reserves page space through data-sf-drawer-dock-host.
Existing modal and modeless behavior is unchanged when docked is absent.
Escape already handled by an editor or drag (defaultPrevented) does not close the drawer.
Drawer is scoped to docked and modeless workspace panels.
The modal mode stays the default for compatibility but is deprecated; use sf-modal with position="inline-start|inline-end" for modal side panels.
drawer:* events bubble and are composed, so hosts can listen on the document; detail.drawer names the emitting drawer.
onBeforeOpen, onAfterOpen, onBeforeClose and onAfterClose still receive only that drawer's own events.
Ancestor listeners added with addEventListener now also see events of nested drawers; check event.detail.drawer.

A docked drawer without the room (dock host or window narrower than its dock-breakpoint) floats over the page as a modal panel: scrim, focus kept inside, page lock, Escape, focus returned to its opener. A docked column is unchanged.
modal="false" on a docked drawer keeps it modeless when it floats, as before.
A modal drawer's Tab cycle runs through the panel and then its edge (close, copy-link, open-full of sf-property-view); a focus on the edge counts as inside.
